body:
- **FY25 (promoter-led):** tone was very upbeat ("light at the end of the tunnel", "Q4 turnaround", "worst is behind us") while delivery was poor on every near-term number. Tone was well above delivery, which is the pattern the India research (Jain, Khizer & Thirumalai) calls cheap talk.
- **FY26–27 (COO/CEO-led):** numeric tone is measured and is beaten every time, so the tone-delivery gap is negative, which is good. Execution tone is still "on track / absolutely on track / in line with planned schedule" while timelines slip, so that gap is still large.
- **Confound.** The change in leadership coincides with the turn in the cycle. These data cannot separate "a better guider" from "a guide set in a rising market". The cycle/execution split gives the same answer in both eras: execution items under-deliver whoever is speaking.

body:
**Set:** 131 case_study records → **106 company-episodes** (43 traps: 19 fraud, 15 leverage/business blow-ups,
9 busts after a winning run; 63 winners incl. 9 false-alarm-only episodes) after merging duplicates; 14
records excluded (funds, sector/market cycles, private companies, Waaree/Premier = neither). Every record id is
covered (script checks). Mechanical data existed before T for only ~45% of episodes: most long-run winners start
in 2003–2013, before screener's 12-year window, and US XBRL starts ~2009.

**Big caveat — this set is in-sample.** The hard disqualifiers were *written from* these very trap cases
(insight:disqualifiers, L10/L12). Strict pre-T dating removes most of the circularity, but the judgment flags
(H1b, H1c) were still coded by someone who knows the outcome, and winners' records list no "tells", so H1b/H1c
were never seriously searched for on winners. Read the hard-rule catch rates as an *upper bound*.

body:
- 2026-11-22: feasibility done (13/15). Frame built (`s1_frame.py`): D 1,739 census, X 500 of 2,132, L 900 of 5,070.
  Page phase started; pre-registration above saved before the chart phase.
- 2026-11-22 (resumed after a usage-limit pause): pages (3,139 companies, ~82 min), charts (1,345) and schedules (322)
  fetched at ≥ 1.55 s per request from one stream. **Process slip:** a chained job started the chart and schedule
  phases early, so about 32 chart and 6 schedule requests ran alongside the page stream for about a minute (two
  streams). All later fetching was single-stream. All files are cached under the scratchpad `bt_solv_in/`.
- **Deviation found on audit, before the verdict table was read:** dead or merged banks with unlabeled screener pages
  (Oriental Bank, Allahabad, Andhra, State Bank of Mysore / Travancore, Lakshmi Vilas) escaped
  `solvency_screen.is_financial()`, whose label fallback looks only for "Financing Profit". Fix in `s3_panel.py`: an
  unlabeled page with a "Deposits" row or "Bank" in the name counts as financial (10 rows removed; 499 → 489). This
  follows the pre-registered exclusion, so it is not a change of rule. Verdicts are the same before and after the fix
  (before it, S5 was 2.00 [1.04, 3.12], also a question at two decimals). The live screen faces the same gap only for
  label-less pages.
